title: Isolation of Primary Murine Retinal Ganglion Cells (RGCs) by Flow Cytometry
protocol: Autoclave all dissection instruments.
Store autoclaved dissection instruments in a sterile area.
Use 4 standard forceps (2 long, 2 short) for dissection.
Use 2 scissors for dissection.
Keep an extra set of forceps and scissors as backup.
Prepare 100 mL of sterile PBS/1% FBS solution.
Chill the PBS/1% FBS solution at 4 °C.
Do not add sodium azide to the solution.
Prepare PBS/1% FBS by mixing 99 mL of PBS with 1 mL of FBS.
Prepare 100 mL of sterile neural cell medium supplemented with 3% FBS.
Chill collection tubes pre-coated with 5 mL of collection medium by placing them in an ice bucket.
Place 40-mm dishes, 70-µm nylon strainers, syringes, pestles for the cell strainer, and sterile polypropylene tubes in the biosafety cabinet.
Euthanize mice using CO2 inhalation followed by cervical dislocation.
Insert forceps under the globe of the eye, grip the optic nerve, and pull up.
Place collected eyes in a vial containing PBS.
Keep the vial on ice until the next step.
Dissect each eye individually under the base plate of a dissection microscope.
Hold the globe at the optic nerve base using forceps.
Use a 30-gauge sharp needle to puncture the cornea to allow aqueous humor evacuation.
Hold the cornea with forceps and use scissors to make a small incision in the cornea.
Gently peel the cornea and sclera using forceps.
Roll the retina and lens out using forceps when the globe is peeled halfway.
Discard the cornea, sclera, and lens.
Place the retina in a small 40-mm Petri dish containing PBS/1% FBS.
Wash each retina three times with fresh sterile PBS/1% FBS within the biosafety cabinet.
Place up to 12 retinae on a sterile 70-µm nylon strainer moistened with PBS/1% FBS.
Gently macerate the retinae using the back-end of a 10-mL syringe in a circular motion to detach cells.
Alternatively, use enzymatic digestion with 15 IU/mL papain, 5 mM L-cysteine, and 200 U/mL DNase I for 15 min at 37 °C.
Inactivate the enzymatic solution with PBS/10% FBS.
Place the sterile 70-µm nylon strainer over a polypropylene collection tube.
Pass collected cells through the strainer using a P1000 pipette.
Rinse the strainer with PBS/1% FBS to release remaining cells and transfer them to the collection tube.
Add PBS/1% FBS to achieve a final volume of 1 mL per retina.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 7 min at 200 x g and room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in PBS/1% FBS using a ratio of 1 mL per 5 retinae.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Clean a glass hemocytometer and coverslip with 70% alcohol.
Gently swirl the tube containing the cells to ensure even distribution of the retina cell suspension.
Mix 20 µL of 0.4% trypan blue with 20 µL of the cell suspension.
Apply 10 µL of the 0.4% trypan blue/cell suspension mix to the hemocytometer, filling both chambers.
Count all trypan blue-negative cells using a microscope; this number represents live cells.
Determine cell viability using the formula: live cell count / total cell count = % viability.
If cell viability is less than 95%, use a fluorescent viability dye for cell viability discrimination during FACS.
Wash the cells with PBS to remove serum traces.
Add 1 µL of fluorescent viability dye per 5.0 x 10^6 cells in a final volume of 100 µL.
Incubate at RT for 15 min, protected from light.
Add 10x the volume of PBS/1% FBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 x g and RT.
If necessary, incubate the cell suspension overnight at 4 °C with neural cell medium in the tube.
Wash cells and maintain them in PBS/1% FBS.
Take a small aliquot of cells (5.0 x 10^6 cells) for negative control use as unlabeled sample.
Add 1 μl of an anti-mouse CD16/32 antibody per 1.0 x 10^6 cells in a 50-μL final volume using PBS/1% FBS.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Prepare the antibody cocktail with CD90.2 AF-700, CD48 PE-Cyanine7, and CD15 PE.
Add the antibody cocktail to the sample and mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate for 30 min in an ice bucket covered from light.
Use 1 µg of CD90.2 AF700 per 5.0 x 10^6 cells.
Use 0.4 µg of CD48 PE-Cyanine7 per 5.0 x 10^6 cells.
Use 0.02 µg of CD15 PE per 5.0 x 10^6 cells.
Use 0.4 µg of un-tagged CD57 per 5.0 x 10^6 cells.
Prepare an antibody cocktail by mixing 80 µL of antibodies in total.
Add 50 µL of anti-mouse CD16/32 to the antibody cocktail.
Mix with 870 µL of PBS/1% FBS to make a final volume of 1,000 µL.
Incubate cells with the antibody cocktail for 30 min.
Wash samples by centrifuging at 200 x g and room temperature for 7 min.
Repeat washing procedure once to remove unbound antibodies.
Add 2 µL of secondary antibody (0.1 µg) per 5.0 x 10^6 cells.
Incubate with the secondary antibody in an ice bucket for 30 min.
Wash cells twice as described previously.
Label cells with secondary antibody if an un-tagged primary antibody was used.
Place 3 drops of polystyrene microspheres into sterile FACS tubes per fluorophore.
Add 1 µg of the respective fluorophore to each tube.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Add 3 mL of PBS/1% FBS to the sample tubes.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 x g and room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend in 250 µL of PBS/1% FBS.
Set up negative controls using polystyrene microspheres that do not bind to Ig.
Have the cell sorting performed by a trained operator.
Ensure the instrument is cleaned and sterilized with 70% ethanol prior to sample acquisition.
Wipe the outside of collection tubes with 70% ethanol.
Pipette cells up and down if they have settled or aggregated.
Filter the suspension through a sterile 40-µm nylon strainer before acquisition.
Control the temperature at 4 °C during cell sorting.
Perform compensation to correct for spectral overlap from the fluorophores.
Select Experiment > Compensation Setup > Create Compensation Controls.
Add the fluorophore-specific controls from the list displayed in the screen.
Click OK.
Use an unlabeled control (no fluorophore) to verify FSC and SSC.
Gate the initial population (P1).
Right-click P1 gate and select Apply to All Compensation Controls.
Install the negative control tube onto the cytometer and click Load.
Verify that the population of interest is displayed and select it.
Record Data for the installed tube.
Unload and remove the tube after recording data.
Repeat steps until all data from the controls have been recorded.
Select Experiment > Compensation Setup > Calculate Compensation.
Save the setup and name the experiment.
Click Link & Save.
Set up P1 by plotting FSC versus SSC.
Draw a pseudocolor plot of SSC-H versus SSC-W using the selected population in step 5.7.1 (P1).
Perform this step to collect single cells only; the single cell gate is called P2.
Repeat step 5.7.2 to plot FSC-H versus FSC-W using P2.
Select all CD90.2+CD48neg cells to eliminate monocytes from the RGC enrichment; call this gate CD90.2+CD48neg, or P3.
Draw a pseudocolor plot of CD57 versus CD15 using the selected CD90.2+CD48neg population or P3 gate.
Gate the CD15negCD57neg population.
Define the populations to be collected for the sample in the "Sort Layout" window.
Proceed with cell sorting; collect the CD90.2+CD48negCD15negCD57neg population.
Perform a purity check using 25,000 cells.
Re-analyze sorted cells to verify the effectiveness of the sort.
Fix sorted cells for 1 h.
Permeabilize cells at 4 °C to inactivate metabolism and allow antibody penetration.
Dilute anti-RNA binding protein with multiple splicing (RBPMS) at a 1:100 dilution in the permeabilization solution.
Dilute anti-synuclein gamma (SNCG) at a 1:100 dilution in the permeabilization solution.
Dilute brain-specific homeobox/POU domain protein 3A (BRN3A) at a 1:100 dilution in the permeabilization solution.
Dilute anti-neuron-specific class III beta tubulin (TUJ1) at a 1:100 dilution in the permeabilization solution.
Incubate cells and antibody solutions for 1 h in an ice bucket covered.
Wash samples twice with PBS/1% FBS.
Resuspend cells in AF488-tagged secondary antibody at a 1:200 dilution for 30 min in an ice bucket.
Wash the samples as previously done.
Keep cells in PBS/1% FBS (250 μL) until analysis.
Extract RNA from 5.0 x 10^5 sorted cells by cell lysis and homogenization followed by chloroform addition.
Transfer the upper, colorless phase to a clean microtube for alcohol precipitation.
Concentrate extract using a spin column.
Perform DNAse digestion on the column.
Wash the column with RNase-free water for RNA elution.
Assess RNA concentration by spectrophotometry.
Synthesize cDNA and perform pre-amplification.
Use 100 ng of RNA material.
Mix with a solution containing reverse transcriptase enzyme, recombinant ribonuclease inhibitor, magnesium chloride (MgCl2), and deoxynucleotides.
Incubate the tube contents for 10 min at 25 °C.
Incubate for an additional 60 min at 42 °C.
Finish the reaction with a 5-min incubation at 85 °C.
Store the resulting cDNA at -20 °C until ready to use.
Pre-amplify cDNA material using a series of primers specific for multiple retinal cell types.
Prepare the pre-amplification reaction in a final volume of 10 µL containing 2.5 µL of cDNA, reverse transcriptase enzyme, and nuclease-free water.
Carry out the enzyme activation step at 95 °C for 10 min.
Perform 14 cycles with each cycle consisting of 95 °C for 15 s followed by 60 °C for 4 min.
Dilute the pre-amplified material 1:10 in Tris EDTA buffer.
Store diluted pre-amplified material at -20 °C until ready for use.
Prepare all qPCR reactions in a 10 µL final volume using diluted, pre-amplified cDNA.
Include primers, nuclease-free water, and a concentrate with DNA polymerase and deoxynucleotides.
Run the qPCR on an instrument starting with a hold step of 50 °C for 2 min.
Continue with a step at 95 °C for 10 min.
Repeat 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s followed by 60 °C for 1 min.
Perform all measurements in triplicates.
Use the comparative CT method to quantify results after determining CT values for housekeeping and target genes.
Calculate relative fold change (Rq) using Rq = 2^(-∆CT), where ∆CT is CT target gene – CT reference gene.
